hints: Differentiate $x=\sqrt t+3$ and $y=\ln t$ separately with respect to $t$.
Divide $1/t$ by $\tfrac12t^{-1/2}$ and simplify the power of $t$.
The tangent and normal gradients have product $-1$, so a normal gradient of $-2$ requires a tangent gradient of $\frac12$.
Use $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt t}$ from part (a) and solve $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt t}=\dfrac12$ for $t>0$.
Substitute that parameter value into both $x=\sqrt t+3$ and $y=\ln t$, keeping the coordinates exact.
walkthrough:
Use the perpendicular relation between the gradient of the normal $m_N$ and the gradient of the tangent $m_T$:
$$m_T = -\dfrac{1}{m_N} = -\dfrac{1}{-2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Set $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ using the result from part (a):
$$\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{t}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\sqrt{t} = 4$$
$$t = 16$$

State the exact coordinates of the point:
$$(7, \ln 16) \quad (\text{or } (7, 4\ln 2))$$
